answer: At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a river tag. The copper cap is enforced at intake and sparrow makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, because every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
